singleSourced.context: In a comment made during the second quarter earnings briefing, Zelnick commented that—despite GTA 6 not officially being released for another week—its launch trajectory is "tracking far above our initial expectations" in terms of preorder volume.
Some analysts believe the game will sell more than 50 million copies in its first year, which may mean that even potentially lofty expectations could be exceeded.

Related:The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time exceeds 5 million copies sold in first week

Backing up the publisher's optimism is confirmation from PlayStation that Grand Theft Auto VI is officially the most pre-ordered game in the history of the PlayStation store, presumably since the store opened in 2006, but likewise did not share direct numbers.

In other Take-Two financial news, GTA 6's predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, reached 235 million copies sold in the last quarter, pushing the overall franchise numbers for the entire Grand Theft Auto series to 480 million units.

Net bookings and net revenue for the company are down overall for the quarter ending September 30, 2026 when compared to the year prior, largely owed to a slow start for NBA 2K27, which Zelnick explains away in an interview with IGN as suffering from proximity to Grand Theft Auto VI.

This year, Take-Two reported $1.6 billion in net bookings, down $276.8 million and 1.2 percent shy of targets, while net revenue came in at $1.497 billion, down $276.8 million and slightly above forecasts.
